quote: Anyway, buddy. I just changed company. I was at BKV Energy, but I'm changing over to Four Change Energy, I think, is the name of the company.
stewart_read: Customer switched utility providers only two days prior. The bill data captured later in the call (usage history, $7 bill from a 1-2 day billing cycle) reflects the OLD provider's account, not the new one — a data-quality issue for system design accuracy.
coaching_implication: Flag for the closer: the usage history captured is from BKV Energy, not the new Four Change Energy account. Confirm which provider's data the design should be built from, or whether a fresh bill is needed once the new account has billing history.

quote: which is one of the reasons I wanna go with solar. But Mhmm. Should I put the pool the pool before solar panels or the solar panels first?
stewart_read: A planned pool addition is a direct future-load enthusiasm signal — it will materially raise the customer's usage and strengthens the case for a larger system. The rep noted it for the file but didn't reflect it back as a reason solar makes even more sense now.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verbally tie the pool to system sizing in the moment (e.g., 'that's great context, we'll want to size for that increased usage') rather than only logging it — reinforces the customer's own stated motivation.

quote: It's hard to put the solar panels first. I'll just put that in the notes for you, though, so we can make sure to include that.
stewart_read: A brief, reasonable sequencing answer to a logistics question, not a meaningful scope violation — the rep gave a light directional answer and immediately deferred detail to notes/specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as minor scope creep since sequencing advice edges toward closer-tier content.
coaching_implication: No real coaching action needed here; if anything, model this as an example of answering briefly then punting detail to the specialist.

quote: I'm I'm still trying to do this. Okay. I'm not a very technical savvy person.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly names his own tech friction. Schema's low-tech pivot calls for a fast move to verbal read-back within about two minutes; the rep instead persisted through photo/text channel-switching for several more minutes before the customer self-solved.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic patience: the rep may have judged the customer was close to succeeding and let him try rather than interrupting his momentum.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to offer the read-back option explicitly at the first sign of friction ('no worries, you can also just read me the numbers off the graph') rather than waiting for the customer to work it out alone.

quote: I was actually referred to Ion by one of y'all's customers. I will have to get her name for you.
stewart_read: A live referral lead is valuable pipeline information, but the rep's response was a flat acknowledgment rather than capturing any concrete referral-program next step beyond deferring to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Deferring to the specialist is schema-consistent scope discipline, not a miss, since referral processing may be a closer-stage task.
coaching_implication: Confirm with Kenny whether setters have any referral-capture responsibility beyond noting it for the specialist; if not, this is a non-issue and should be dropped from future scoring.

quote: just to go over all the information. I will be Mhmm. I will be out of town Uh-huh. Thursday through Tuesday of next week. I won't be able to answer the phone, and I'll be out of country.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a hard multi-day unavailability window right before the appointment is booked. The rep booked for 'tomorrow' (April 15) at 5pm, which appears to fall before the Thursday-through-Tuesday window, but the rep never explicitly confirmed the booked slot was clear of that window — it was left implicit rather than verified aloud.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have done the date math silently and correctly, since tomorrow falls before the stated Thursday-start travel window.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verbally close the loop on travel conflicts even when the math seems to work — e.g., 'that's before you leave, so we're good' — so the confirmation is explicit for both customer and any handoff record, rather than assumed.

quote: And then I'll be sure to send you a text message with the details of this appointment as well just so you can put that on your schedule and have a better reminder.
stewart_read: Rep delivers the text-follow-up promise, one required button-up element, but the call ends without the 'is that fair' handshake or a restated no-driving/computer instruction.
coaching_implication: Add the missing button-up elements (computer/no-driving framing, explicit fairness handshake) as a quick script-completeness note for this rep.
